items.q: How do listeners unconsciously rank every speaker?
items.a: Into **rookie**, **pretty good**, or **natural** — judged on **voice, body language, and words**. Diagnose yourself on that map before practicing random tips.

items.q: Are bad communicators "bad people," or something else?
items.a: *"You're not a bad communicator. You just have **bad communication habits**."* Tiers are **habits, not identity** — Vinh's ESL/refugee arc proves the future version is trainable.

items.q: What does rookie voice and body usually look like?
items.a: **Flat delivery** (one speed/pitch/volume/emotion), **vocal fry**, fillers every breath, **no expression**, bad posture, awkward eye contact — listeners decode meaning for you.
Record a **2-min answer** to *"Why improve communication?"*, **transcribe** it, then audit **fillers, clarity, and repetition**. Most rookies live in **unconscious incompetence**.

items.q: Can brilliant people still sound like rookies?
items.a: Yes — Vinh cites **Zuckerberg / Musk / Altman** succeeding despite rough delivery. **Mere mortals cannot** lean on brilliance alone; polish is the equalizer.

items.q: What keeps "pretty good" speakers stuck in the middle?
items.a: They have more range but **play it safe** — limited **gesture vocabulary**, **non-functional body language**, and **fear of judgment**. Rebut with the **spotlight effect**: people think about themselves, not you.

items.q: When should you move on stage or in a room?
items.a: **Only move with purpose.** If there's no reason, don't move — stillness is a pro tool. Mark Manson's repetitive pacing is called out as **non-functional** movement.

items.q: What does natural-tier voice actually control?
items.a: All **five vocal foundations** at once: **rate, volume, pitch, tonality, pause**. Face must **sync** with voice — emotion heard but not seen (or RBF) means the audience won't feel it.

items.q: How do naturals structure words beyond winging it?
items.a: Layer **frameworks** (PREP, STAR, **321**, PARA, PEEL) with **stories, analogies, props, and activities** so listeners don't follow your raw thought process — like the "read more books" army/exercise demo.
